raw_responses.Bulgarian:
The figure is a line chart titled “Hidden State Mean,” which visually compares the absolute mean values of hidden states across different neural network layers for three distinct conditions: “before gate,” “after gate,” and “baseline.” The horizontal axis, labeled “Layer,” spans from 0 to approximately 22, with tick marks at intervals of 5 (0, 5, 10, 15, 20), indicating discrete layer indices. The vertical axis, labeled “Abs Mean,” ranges from 0 to 4.5, with major tick marks at intervals of 1 (0, 1, 2, 3, 4), representing the absolute mean magnitude of hidden states. Three data series are plotted: a blue dashed line labeled “hidden state mean before gate, avg 0.71,” which starts near 0.1 at Layer 0, remains relatively flat until Layer 10, then rises gradually to about 0.8 at Layer 15, and sharply increases to over 4.0 by Layer 22; a red dotted line labeled “hidden state mean after gate, avg 0.05,” which stays close to 0 across all layers, with a slight upward trend visible only after Layer 15; and a green solid line labeled “hidden state mean of baseline, avg 0.04,” which remains nearly flat and close to 0 throughout the entire range of layers, with no significant variation. The legend is positioned in the upper left corner and clearly associates each line style and color with its corresponding condition and average value.

raw_responses.English:
The plot illustrates the absolute mean of hidden states across different layers for three distinct conditions: before a gate, after a gate, and a baseline, with each represented by a separate line. The x-axis, labeled “Layer,” spans from 0 to approximately 22, with tick marks at intervals of 5, indicating a linear scale. The y-axis, labeled “Abs Mean,” ranges from 0 to 4.5, also on a linear scale, with major ticks at intervals of 1. The dashed blue line, representing “hidden state mean before gate,” begins near 0.05 at Layer 0, remains relatively flat until Layer 10, then gradually increases to about 0.8 at Layer 20, and sharply rises to approximately 4.4 at Layer 22. The dotted orange line, labeled “hidden state mean after gate,” starts near 0.0 at Layer 0, stays close to zero until Layer 15, then rises slightly to about 0.1 at Layer 22. The solid green line, “hidden state mean of baseline,” remains nearly flat across all layers, hovering just above 0.0, with a slight upward trend reaching approximately 0.1 at Layer 22.

The blue line starts near 0.05, stays flat until Layer 10, rises gradually to 0.8 at Layer 20, then jumps to 4.4 at Layer 22. raw_responses.German:
This line chart, titled "Hidden State Mean," displays the absolute mean of hidden states across different layers for three distinct conditions: "hidden state mean before gate," "hidden state mean after gate," and "hidden state mean of baseline." The x-axis, labeled "Layer," spans from 0 to approximately 22, with tick marks at intervals of 5, indicating a linear scale representing discrete layer indices. The y-axis, labeled "Abs Mean," ranges from 0 to 4, also on a linear scale, and quantifies the absolute mean value of the hidden states. The first data series, "hidden state mean before gate," is represented by a blue dashed line with circular markers; it begins near 0.1 at Layer 0, fluctuates slightly between 0.2 and 0.4 up to Layer 18, then rises sharply to approximately 2.6 at Layer 21 and peaks at about 4.3 at the final layer. The second series, "hidden state mean after gate," shown as a red dotted line with circular markers, remains near 0 across all layers, with a slight upward trend toward the end, reaching approximately 0.1 at Layer 22. The third series, "hidden state mean of baseline," depicted as a solid green line with circular markers, stays consistently near 0 throughout, with minor fluctuations not exceeding 0.1.
